name: Die Hard
text: All Critical Wounds can be healed. For Toughness Bonus Rounds after death, at the start of each Round make a Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test. On success, return to life with 1 Wound.
adaptation: User-supplied older-edition definition retained; no direct Fifth Edition equivalent.

name: Corrupting Vomit
text: Those hit by a Chaos Troll’s vomit risk exposure to Corruption (Moderate).

name: Rotten Regeneration
text: Use core Regeneration, but the Wounds restored are 1d10 divided by 2, rounded down (Tribes and Tribulations p. 88).

name: Bileful Vomit
text: The Troll’s Vomit follows core Stream of Corruption: CN: 9 Range: Special Target: Special Duration: Instant Your maw distends horrifically before you vomit forth a foul stream of diseased filth and horror. Immediately make an Unopposed Acid- and Poison-type Breath attack (see page 357). It counts as a magic missile with a Damage equal to your Toughness Bonus, and it ignores Armour Points. Further, any targets that take more than their TB in Wounds must pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test or contract Blood Rot (see page 179).

name: That’s No Mound
text: The Troll has Stealthy only while it has not moved or taken an Action.

name: Sated
text: After consuming a creature of Average Size or larger in peace, the Hungry Troll template no longer applies.

name: Starving
text: If the Hungry Troll does not eat within 24 hours it begins to suffer Starvation.

name: Water Wise
text: While within a body of water, the River Troll Hag does not suffer from Stupid. Stupid otherwise remains active.

name: Purple Skullback Bite
text: A creature wounded and Poisoned by this bite takes an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test or gains 1 Corruption point. A Forest Goblin Shaman still takes damage and poison, but for 2d10 hours gains a printed +2d10 bonus to Channelling and Language (Magick), and may reroll Waaagh! Miscast results. Situational bonuses are not added permanently.
adaptation: Printed Average (+20) uses core Average (+2 SL); current Venom inflicts Poisoned on Wounds without an avoidance Test.
